Q1: Iron(II) sulfate is categorized with known oral hazards (Tier 1). Expanded perspectives indicate potential carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive, and environmental hazards, as well as dermal and eye hazards (Tier 2). Data is currently deficient regarding endocrine disruption, inhalation, and organ and systemic hazards (Tier 4).
Q2: This chemical is listed as a hazardous substance under the Clean Water Act, indicating potential dangers upon discharge into waterways. However, it is also on the FDA's GRAS list, suggesting that its low hazard designation likely applies to very low quantities under specific, tightly regulated conditions.
Q3: Iron(II) sulfate is extensively studied, with 81,000 literature references and 66 toxicity value records, indicating significant research attention. While its molecular structure is well-defined, it lacks formal comprehensive EPA assessments (IRIS or PPRTV) and has several hazard classes where data remains deficient.
